done_when: On Windows, codex.identity reads a process's start time and executable path through the Windows API with ctypes (OpenProcess, GetProcessTimes, QueryFullProcessImageNameW) instead of running PowerShell, so no child process is started; identity keeps its contract (None when no process has the id, a matching record otherwise, and a reused id never matches); POSIX is unchanged; a test on Windows exercises a live process, an exited one and a mismatch

findings.body: On Windows, removing this guard lets an empty record reach `_alive({})`, which returns `None` (src/forge/codex.py:472–475), followed by `recorded["pid"]` at line 495, raising `KeyError`. This happens on the first `forge work`/`read`, because `hold()` calls `_stop_leftover()` before any record exists (line 532), and when `app_server` is null. The exception also interrupts lock cleanup in `hold()`'s finally block. Keep an explicit check for absent process records when bypassing the command-name check.
findings.title: Handle absent process records before checking Windows leftovers

findings.body: The existing Windows suite still requires the old command-line representation and PowerShell interception. In tests/test_codex_record.py:255, `test_5_one_worker_per_item` unconditionally expects `codex_turn` in the driver's command, but this return now supplies the Python executable path. Lines 263–269 also expect a PowerShell stub to create an observation file, and lines 275–283 use PowerShell failures to test unreadable identities; those stubs are no longer called. These cases run in the Windows suite (.github/workflows/forge-next.yml:23–36). Update their assertions and failure scenarios for native identity, preserving the behaviors they protect; fixing the empty-record crash alone will still leave CI failing.
findings.title: Not done: Windows process-record tests exercise native identity

findings.body: The mismatch and exited-process cases inspect only missing output and a deleted lock, so both accept an unexpected exception as success. In this branch, neither case creates a process-record JSON file, so `doctor` reaches the empty-record `KeyError` in `_stop_leftover()`. `tidy()` nevertheless deletes the lock in its finally block (src/forge/codex.py:597–607), satisfying these assertions while recovery crashes. Assert that doctor completes its normal reporting path and has no unexpected traceback, accounting for the fixture's expected configuration diagnostics.
findings.title: Not done: Windows identity test rejects doctor crashes

why: On Windows, Forge's process check (codex.identity) shells out to PowerShell Get-CimInstance, and CI shows that call sometimes never returns: a pytest worker hung in subprocess communicate() during crash recovery (test_codex_resume.py test_9), like the earlier Windows hang in test_4
